title: Honey Garlic Salmon
subtitle: pan-seared salmon in a sticky honey garlic butter glaze, with rice & broccoli
imageAlt: Honey garlic glazed salmon fillet with white rice and broccoli
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Soy sauce, lemon juice, garlic & spices

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen salmon? Thaw in the fridge overnight, or sealed in cold water for about 1 hour.
Start the rice first — 15 minutes plus a 10 minute rest.
Mix the glaze before the salmon goes in; honey and garlic burn fast once they hit the pan.

items.name: salmon fillets
items.note: 4 pieces about 225 g each, skin on or off

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Bring the rice, water, salt and butter to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on, then fluff.

steps.title: Mix the glaze & season
steps.text: Stir the honey, soy sauce, lemon juice and garlic together. Pat the salmon dry and season with salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika.

steps.title: Steam the broccoli
steps.text: Steam or boil the broccoli 4–5 minutes until bright green and just tender. Drain and season with a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Sear the salmon
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high. Lay the salmon in presentation-side down (skin side up) and leave it alone 4 minutes until golden and it releases easily. Flip.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium. Add the butter and the glaze and let it bubble 2–3 minutes, spooning it over the salmon as it thickens, until the thickest part reads 63°C (145°F) and flakes easily. Turn the heat down if the glaze darkens too fast.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate the salmon on the rice with the broccoli and spoon the extra glaze from the pan over everything.

fixIt.fix: It wasn't ready to flip. Leave it another minute — it lets go on its own when the crust forms. A non-stick pan helps.
Heat was too high. Lower to medium the moment the glaze goes in; it only needs 2–3 minutes.
Take the salmon out and simmer the glaze 1 more minute, then spoon it over.
Pull it at 63°C (145°F) — thinner tail pieces are done sooner, so check those first.

saleTip: Fresh Atlantic salmon is around $13/lb regular at No Frills but often drops to $9–10/lb. Frozen salmon portions (e.g. 908 g bag) are usually cheaper and work great — thaw overnight.
swap: Use frozen salmon portions to bring it to $$ (~$25). Shrimp works too (2 min per side).
leftovers: Fridge 2 days (fish is best fresh). Eat cold over rice, or reheat gently, covered, at 50% power so it doesn't dry out.
doneness: Salmon: 63°C (145°F) in the thickest part; it should flake easily.
source: Based on tested pan-seared honey garlic salmon methods (sear then glaze, 145°F); safe temp per Health Canada.
